accuracy.evidence: Persistence is framed as the EYFS Development Matters characteristic of effective learning (keep on trying when challenges occur, bounce back after difficulties) and matches the topic's three evidence statements: stay with a hard task, try a different approach after a mistake, talk about difficulty positively. The adult text avoids the overclaim that mindset slogans alone raise attainment and cites the small average effects found in the Sisk et al. 2018 meta-analysis. The beanbag model is physically honest: equal power lands in the same spot and more power lands further.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented slips: treating a mistake as proof of being bad at something (challenge 'mistake', m1, sorter), repeating the identical attempt and calling it persistence (same power twice is refused with 'same place: change something', challenge 'change', m2), believing skill is fixed ('some kids just can't ride' in the bike prediction, challenge 'practise', m5), confusing a calm break with quitting (tower step, visual sorter, m3, p4), comparing with faster peers (challenge 'speed', m4), and persisting alone for ever instead of asking for a clue (challenge 'ask', m7).

lab_distinct.evidence: Four mechanisms no other lab has: a power-controlled beanbag throw where every miss is marked too short or too far on the grass; a five-day practice calendar that grows a falling wobble chart while 'skip practice' leaves it unchanged; a thought-sorting step where each correctly sorted stop thought is rewritten by Pip into its 'yet' version and an energy bar fills; and a tower that topples whenever a wider block goes on a narrower one, locked until a breathing balloon lowers a cross meter. The shingle gate passed against all flagship labs, including flaghelp.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner finds the rules by doing: throws converge only when they change power in the direction the clue says; the wobble bars drop day by day only when they practise; Pip will not build while the cross meter is high, so the break is felt as the thing that makes the next try possible; and the tray order (small, big, middle) makes the naive left-to-right attempt fail, so the second, changed attempt (big at the bottom) is what works. The step text only confirms what just happened.

predictions.evidence: Four locked predictions, each with a tempting wrong option that the task then disproves: 'throw the same way again' after a short throw (the lab refuses an identical throw), 'some kids just can't ride' (the chart shrinks to zero wobbles), the words 'never' or 'ever' instead of 'yet', and 'stop building for ever' or 'kick the blocks' after a fall (the calm break plus a new order builds the tower).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven rotating challenge kinds (mistake, change, yet, break, practise, speed, ask) with answer order rotated. Eleven distinct feedback messages each name the slip and the fix, for example 'The same try gives the same result. Change something', 'Hiding a mistake hides the clue', 'Skills grow with practice. Pip wobbled at first too', and 'Then they do the learning, not you'. Correct answers build a star streak; a miss resets it.

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs use one- and two-syllable words in very short sentences ('A mistake is a clue.', 'Feel cross? Take a break.') and pass the family kid limit of FK 5.0; lab text is a single short line per state. The adult section stays within FK 10 and gives a concrete routine: pick something a little too hard, ask what the mistake says to change, name new strategies aloud.

no_filler.evidence: Each kid paragraph carries one idea (hard means learning, mistakes are clues and change the try, yet, calm break). Each adult paragraph has one job: definition with source, the two key ideas, named mistakes with the evidence caveat, and the home routine. No step in the lab repeats another; the sandbox reuses the throw with new bucket spots to practise the clue rule.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at iPhone 13 (390 px) in dark and light themes for every step: calendar boxes, chart labels, thought zones (wrapped to two lines), blocks and balloon are all inside the canvas with nothing clipped after moving the chart title and Pip clear of the bike. The young class gives 56 px buttons; the beanbag drag works with touch and a pull of 14 px per power step.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button twin (Softer, Harder, Throw with the current power, Practise day N, Skip, Keeps/Stops, Breathe, Stack each block), the canvas aria-label is rewritten after each action with power, landing result, day and wobble count, energy or cross meter, and the challenge feedback sits in a polite live region. The walkthrough's axe scan was clean in both themes on desktop and phone.
